# NOTES

## Pi Session File Format (pi.dev)

Pi stores every conversation as a *...[trimmed]

This project — **`pi-format-demo`** — is a small, deliberately minimal Go project whose sole purpose is to generate a real-world pi session JSONL file.

What's in it:
- **`README.md`** — one-line description.
- **`src/main.go`** — a minimal Go program that prints `Hello from Pi`.
- **`src/TODO.txt`** — a leftover TODO (`build a greeting app`).

The point isn't the code itself; it's to exercise the pi coding agent in a real working directory so the resulting session file (stored under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--…pi-format-demo--/…`) becomes a concrete, real-world example of pi's session format.

`NOTES.md` documents that format in detail: pi saves every conversation as a JSONL **session** (a tree of entries linked by `id`/`parentId`, enabling in-place branching). It covers the file location, the v1/v2/v3 evolution, the `session` header, entry types (`message`, `model_change`, `compaction`, `branch_summary`, `custom`, `label`, etc.), the AgentMessage roles (user/assistant/toolResult/bashExecution/custom/…), content blocks (text/image/thinking/toolCall), how context is rebuilt leaf→root while honoring compaction, and the distinction between `/tree` (same file), `/fork` (new file), and `/clone` (new file).

So: it's a throwaway demo project used as a vehicle to produce an authentic example of pi's session-file format.
